topic: Solutions, Solubility, Acids, Bases, and Salts
key_concepts: Solubility is the amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a giv
Substances may be very soluble, slightly soluble, or insoluble.
Solubility is affected by nature of solute and solvent, temperature, stirring, particle si
Heating a solution generally allows more solute to dissolve.
The rule “like dissolves like” means a solvent dissolves solutes of similar type.
Stirring and smaller particle size make solutes dissolve faster.
Pressure affects the solubility of gases such as carbon dioxide in soft drinks.
Oil and water do not mix because their molecular nature is different.
Acids have pH less than 7 and turn blue litmus paper red.
Bases neutralize acids, have pH greater than 7, and turn red litmus paper blue.
Salts are produced by the reaction of an acid with a base.
